## Fixed

- **Restoring a full backup deleted every user account and restored none — then
  reported success.** Backups have always been written with password hashes
  stripped out, but the restore only re-created accounts that *had* a password
  hash. Since none ever did, a restore deleted the whole user table and put
  nothing back: every account, role and company assignment gone, the system
  dropped to zero users, and the app fell back to the first-run setup wizard.
  The response still said the restore had succeeded, so nothing about it looked
  wrong until someone tried to sign in. If a backup can't restore accounts, it
  now leaves the existing ones alone and says so.
- **Restoring a backup from the Saved Backups list failed completely.** The
  server-side restore had the same code as the upload restore but without the
  check above, so any saved backup containing at least one user hit a database
  error, rolled the whole restore back, and returned only "Restore failed". That
  path is the one scheduled backups feed, so it was broken in exactly the
  situation it exists for. Both restores now run the same code, so they can't
  drift apart again.
- **Companies and per-user company access were never backed up at all.** A
  restore could therefore not rebuild who can see which company, and student
  records depended on the companies happening to already exist on the target
  system with the same internal ids. Both are now included, and companies are
  matched by name so a restore works even when two systems number them
  differently.

## Added

- **"Include user credentials" when creating a backup.** Off by default. With
  it, the archive carries the password hashes and MFA secrets a restore needs to
  bring accounts back on a rebuilt server — so it's only offered for an archive
  that will actually be encrypted (a standard backup needs `ENCRYPTION_KEY`
  set; a portable backup is always passphrase-encrypted). Such a file is
  equivalent to the password database, so store it accordingly. Scheduled
  backups have the same option in the Automatic Backups panel.
- MFA secrets are re-encrypted with the target system's key during a restore, so
  a portable backup restored onto a machine with a different encryption key
  leaves multi-factor sign-in working instead of locking those users out.
- A restore that would leave the system with **no enabled SuperAdmin** is now
  refused before anything is changed, rather than completing and locking
  everyone out of administration.

## Updated

- **The restore result now tells you what happened to user accounts** — how many
  the archive held, how many were restored and how many were skipped, plus the
  companies and access assignments — and shows an amber warning rather than a
  green tick when no accounts could be restored.
- Restoring accounts now signs you out, because the restored accounts aren't the
  ones the current session was issued for. Sign in again with an account from
  the backup.
- Companies are never deleted during a restore. One already present is reused
  and one that's missing is created, so scheduled exports, offerings and
  API-key grants that point at them are left intact.

## Note for anyone reading the API directly

`counts.users` in the restore response changed from a plain number (which
reported the archive's row count, not what was actually restored — the reason
this went unnoticed) to `{ inArchive, restored, skipped }`. `counts.companies`
and `counts.userCompanies` are new.
